summary: The redirect/start suite covers the most dangerous invariants well: one-execution-per-pair (redirect_mutatesExistingRow_noSecondExecutionInserted), anti-IDOR CAS (redirect_mismatchedSubscriber_isNoOp), CAS-loss no-op with a real ListAppender WARN assertion (redirect_casLost_isNoOp_andEmitsWarn), broken-cursor terminal-fail with a live 'other execution still runs' control (redirect_brokenCursor_terminalFailsOnlyThatExecution), and the EMIT_EVENT self-loop budget gate (emitEventTriggerSelfLoop_terminatesAtBudgetOrMenuPark). DB assertions read actual Mongo state, not mock returns. Two findings prevent a 'passed' verdict: (1) redirect_ofRunningAndWaiting_movesCursor has a litmus-test failure — the assertion proves completion but not that the cursor actually moved to the redirect target (removing the claimForRedirect .set('currentStepId') line leaves the test green); (2) the allowReEnter=false active-in-flight no-op path required by the TDD anchor and acceptance criterion is not covered — the existing test that claims to cover it drives the redirect branch, not the insertAtEntryStep swallow path.

findings.issue: Litmus test failure. The test iterates over [running, waiting] statuses and asserts only reload(execId).getStatus()==completed and sentCount()-before==1. However, the seed graph is s1=sendMessage('orig', next=null) and entry=sendMessage('redirected', next=null), both with no downstream steps. If claimForRedirect does NOT move currentStepId (or moves it to the wrong step), drive() starts at s1, sends 'orig', hits next=null, and completes with exactly one send. So the assertion passes even with a broken claimForRedirect. Deleting the '.set("currentStepId", entryStepId)' line from the CAS update (FunnelExecutionEngine.java line ~416) leaves both loop iterations green — the test does not prove the cursor moved.

replacement.approach: Shape s1 --next--> tail (two sends if drive() starts at s1) vs entry --> End (one send). The cursor-move is then provable by send count AND the terminal currentStepId.
replacement.concreteChange: Change: FunnelStep s1 = sendMessageStep("s1", "orig", "tail"); FunnelStep tail = sendMessageStep("tail", "orig-tail", null); FunnelStep entry = sendMessageStep("entry", "redirected", null). Seed cursor on s1, enqueueOk(2) as buffer. After redirectExecution: assert sentCount()-before == 1 (entry only, NOT s1+tail) AND reload(execId).getCurrentStepId() == null (entry had no next -> End). This makes the .set(currentStepId) CAS the lone gate between 1 vs 2 sends.
assertions: assertThat(sentCount() - before).isEqualTo(1)         // entry only, NOT s1+tail

findings.location: FunnelEventServiceIT.java — allowReEnter=false active in-flight start path (TDD anchor: event_noInFlight_startsFreshAtEntryStep_respectingAllowReEnter)
findings.issue: The TDD anchor and task-5 acceptance criterion both require: 'allowReEnter=false with an active in-flight execution -> no-op (swallow)'. No test exercises this path. The existing test event_noInFlight_allowReEnterFalse_terminalRowDoesNotBlockFreshInsert uses a terminal (completed) execution — which does NOT hold the running|waiting partial-unique re-enter index — so insertExecutionAt SUCCEEDS (returns true, line ~348), and the swallow catch at line ~349 is never reached. This is the only gap in the start-branch coverage. The dispatch comment and Edge-cases note confirm terminal rows do NOT hold the index, so the swallow is only reachable via a concurrent insert or an active (running|waiting|waiting_for_reply) duplicate row.
findings.recommendation: Option A (IT): seed an event funnel with allowReEnter=false. Seed a RUNNING execution for (funnelId, subscriberId) via seedInFlightExecution. The in-flight probe will find it → the code takes the REDIRECT branch, not the start branch. To force the start-path swallow, the test must ensure inFlightExecutionId returns null (e.g., set the existing row to a terminal status after seeding so the probe misses it), then call dispatchForSubscriber. The concurrent duplicate-key that fires on insertExecutionAt cannot be driven deterministically in an IT. Option B (unit, recommended): in FunnelEventServiceTest add a test: stub eventFunnel('ev','purchase','entry') with allowReEnter=false, mongoTemplate.findOne returns null (no in-flight), doThrow(new DuplicateKeyException("race")).when(executionFactory).insertExecutionAt(any(), any(), any(), any(), anyInt(), eq("entry")). Dispatch event 'purchase'. Assert: (a) LOG_DISPATCH_REENTER_IGNORED logged at WARN or INFO, (b) no exception escapes, (c) fan-out counted=false (redirectOrStart returned false). This locks the entry-step swallow contract symmetrically with the existing step-0 swallow test (reEnter_duplicateOnOneFunnel_doesNotAbortOtherMatches).
findings.note: The existing unit test reEnter_duplicateOnOneFunnel_doesNotAbortOtherMatches stubs insertExecution (the step-0 insertOneFunnel path) on a funnel with triggers==null, so matchedEntryStepId returns null and routing takes insertOneFunnel, NOT insertAtEntryStep. The two LOG_DISPATCH_REENTER_IGNORED emission sites (lines ~492 and ~350) are structurally distinct and both should be locked.

findings.issue: The defensive WARN at the bottom of matchedEntryStepId (fired when a multikey-matched funnel has no in-memory trigger element that re-scans — an unexpected drift) is never tested. It is a greppable operator signal whose logic contains a .equals comparison that could silently regress (e.g. a type-check typo). No test seeds a funnel that is returned by the repository query but whose triggers[] does not match on re-scan.
findings.recommendation: Add a small unit test in FunnelEventServiceTest: stub funnelRepository to return a funnel whose triggers list has only a 'tag_added' element (triggerType mismatch), then dispatch an 'event' type query. Assert LOG_DISPATCH_NO_MATCHED_TRIGGER_ELEMENT WARN fires and insertExecution is called once (fallback start-from-step-0, because entryStepId == null). Ten lines, no new dependencies.

conventionsCheck.notes: The emitEventTriggerSelfLoop test uses warn(appender).stream().anyMatch() || appender.list.stream().anyMatch() — the OR is redundant (both scan the same list for the same constant) but harmless. The LOG_REDIRECT_BROKEN_CURSOR check uses appender.list.anyMatch() without filtering on WARN level — acceptable since the constant is unique.

Both are one-test fixes but must be verified green before the task closes.
